name: Sika Rugasol-90
paste:
SIKA® RUGASOL®-90: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® Rugasol®-90, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sika_rugasol_-90.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® Rugasol®-90 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description.
    - Sika® Rugasol®-90 is a specially formulated liquid surface retarder for summer conditions. Sika® Rugasol®- 90 will cause retardation to the surface of the freshly laid concrete, and can be used to achieve an exposed-aggregate type finish.
    - The retarding compound in Sika® Rugasol®-90 combines with cement at the surface and delays the normal hydration on the surface of the concrete (high cement contents and temperatures will reduce the retardation). After retardation has finished, the concrete cures to its full strength.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sika® Rugasol®-90 can be used on:
    - Driveways
    - Footpaths
    - Patio slabs
    - Beams
    - Architectural concrete

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® Rugasol®-90
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: Concrete surface retarder for horizontal surfaces (Summer)
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Sika® Rugasol®-90 can be used undiluted or in diluted version, depending on the degree of the surface penetration required.
    - Depth of penetration is controlled and constant. Surface retardation of up to 24 hours can be achieved. Extremely cost effective.
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Appearance and colour: Yellow liquid
    - Density: 1.05 kg/l approximately
2.5 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 205 litre drum; 10 litre container
    - Shelf life: Stored at temperatures between 5°C and 35°C in unopened original containers, protected from direct sunlight and frost, shelf life is one (1) year.
    - Storage conditions: Store at temperature between 5°C and 35°C , protected from direct sunlight .

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 Substrate preparation. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) states no substrate preparation requirements.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Consumption. Normal exposure up to 20mm ,coverage is 1 litre/4m2 of surface (undiluted Sika® Rugasol®-90). Normal exposure between 6-10mm, coverage is 1 litre/4m2 of surface (diluted Sika® Rugasol®-90). Note: Dilution rate should be 1 part water to 1 part Sika® Rugasol®-90. Dilution reduces effectiveness of Sika® Rugasol®-90, trials should occur before application
4.3 Application.
    - Sika® Rugasol®-90 should be applied in a good uniform coat onto the horizontal concrete surface as soon as the initial ‘bleeding’ of the concrete has finished but before initial set. (A garden sprayer is suitable). Treated surface should be protected from direct sunlight or warm wind, which can cause the surface to dry out rapidly. Proper curing procedures are important to ensure the durability and quality of the concrete. After the initial set of the concrete has elapsed, typically 2-12 hours, depending on concrete type and ambient conditions such as humidity, temperature and wind the soft cement paste on the surface can be brushed off and the exposed aggregate finish washed down with clean water. Whilst Sika® Rugasol®-90 is in use the concrete surface must be protected from rain, dirt, etc.
    - Spray equipment should be washed out after use with hot water. Subsequent to removal of paste, proper curing should take place with an efficient curing compound such as Sika Antisol .
4.4 Further information.
    - High cement contents and temperatures will reduce the retardation. After retardation has finished, the concrete cures to its full strength.
    - Overdosing will lead to deeper than required expos-ures causing aggregate to dislodge.
    - Concrete must be properly cured to ensure maximum strength development.
    - Bleed water must be removed before application, to prevent product dilution.
    - For additional information, please contact your local Sika Representative.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 01.02) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.4 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® Rugasol®-90, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/j/sika_rugasol_-90.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Rugasol® 90, version 26/06/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/6/sds-rugasol-90.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS RugasolÂ® 90, https://aus.sika.com/dam/dms/au01/0/sds-rugasol-90.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
